state.name: unrecovered_load_pct_seconds
state.description: Load integrated over the time on battery in earlier outages and not yet recovered.

state.name: outage_load_pct_seconds
state.description: Load integrated over the time on battery in the current outage.

state.name: mains_seconds
state.description: Seconds on mains since the last outage ended.

state.name: was_mains_failed
state.description: 1 if the mains input had failed on the previous call, 0 otherwise.

state.name: history_known
state.description: 1 once the battery is known to have recovered, 0 until then. A consumer does not read it.

state.name: last_clock_epoch_seconds
state.description: The time of the previous call, 0 before the first.

parameters.description: Time of the poll as seconds since the Unix epoch, with sub-second precision, identical to the value in the outage record. It is the wall clock and can step, so a model treats a step back as zero seconds elapsed. The text time beside it in the record is not sent.

Load on the UPS output as a whole percent of its rated capacity, as the UPS driver reports it. Not watts: whether the rating is in volt-amperes or watts is not known. When rackmains_read_failures is above 0 it is the last value read.

1 while the UPS is running from its battery because the mains input has failed, 0 on mains. Also 0 during a deliberate battery calibration, when the unit runs from its battery with the mains healthy. Derived by rackmains from the UPS status, which is not sent.
1 during a deliberate battery calibration, when rackmains_mains_failed is held at 0. The battery is discharging when this or rackmains_mains_failed is 1. Absent means 0.
1 while the UPS reports its battery low, meaning it is about to shut down. Not yet observed on this unit: a run to failure will show whether it is raised before the cutoff. Absent means 0.

Battery voltage as the UPS driver reports it, refreshed on each driver poll, every 4 seconds on this host. It sags under load, rebounds when the load drops and sits flat on the plateau until the knee. Absent when the UPS does not report it.
1 while the UPS reports that the battery needs replacing. It does not say the battery was replaced: rackmains_battery_age_days does. Absent means 0.
Whole days since the battery's install date at the poll, back to 0 when that date is edited on a replacement. Absent when the install date is unknown.
Consecutive failed reads of the UPS driver, 0 after a good read. Above 0 the readings sent are the last good ones, so the state keeps integrating while the driver is unreachable. Absent means 0.

The state the model returned on the previous call, carried unchanged by the caller. Absent on the first call, when it arrives as the all-zero vector, which is the initial state with the battery history unknown.
Seconds on battery, accumulated across short dips until the mains has been stable, after which the guard puts the follower servers to sleep. Compared with rackmains_guard_battery_seconds.
Seconds of unbroken mains after which the on-battery clock resets and every server put to sleep is woken. Compared with rackmains_guard_mains_seconds.

Optional. Put the follower servers to sleep when rackmains_battery_runtime_remaining_seconds falls to this: the measured time the shed takes plus a margin. Never above rackmains_guard_shed_battery_seconds.
Optional. Estimated run time left at the current load, rounded down so it never overstates and capped at 86400 seconds. The guard acts on it only with rackmains_guard_shed_runtime_seconds.

Optional. Estimated usable battery energy left as a whole percent, 100 when full, rounded down. Informational: the guard does not act on it. Not the UPS driver's own charge estimate, rackmains_battery_charge_pct.
Optional. Energy the model counts as used since the battery was last full, in the current outage and the unrecovered part of earlier ones.

Optional. 1 when the fit should be redone because it is old, the battery has been replaced or observed drains no longer match its predictions, 0 otherwise. Unrelated to the UPS battery calibration. The reason is rackmains_model_refit_reason_code.
Optional. Why rackmains_model_refit_due is 1: 1 the fit is old, 2 the battery was replaced, 3 observed drains no longer match its predictions. 0 when it is not raised.
Optional. The state to carry to the next call, finite numbers in the slot order of the signature. Absent for a model with no state.
